lab.intro: We are a research group in the School of Energy Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. Our work sits at the interface of nanofluidics and microfluidics: graphene-based desalination, streaming potential, nanofluidic channel fabrication, multiphase microfluidics, droplet dynamics, electrokinetics and the energy performance of buildings.
approach: Molecular dynamics of water, ions and polymers in nanoconfinement: slip, wettability and transport below a micron.
Experiments and simulations of electric double layers, droplets and multiphase flow in micro- and millichannels.
Solar thermal, wind and building energy systems, increasingly guided by machine learning.

pi.name: Dr. Chirodeep Bakli
pi.title: Associate Professor

bio: My research focuses on multiscale fluid flow and heat transfer with the twin objectives to understand the interfacial interactions and flow physics, and to use them to develop smart surfaces and for renewable energy generation.

Part of the research focuses on length scales below micron dimensions, where one has to resort to molecular-level investigations. The results are used to propose a capillary-height-dependent dynamic slip length that explains the filling behaviour in nanocapillaries. For flow in confinement, the interfacial slip was shown to be a complex function of the physical and chemical signature of the solid surface and of the ionic inclusions in the solvent. In a pioneering work, the duality of wettability and slip length was challenged: flow on a hydrophobic surface was optimised to obtain stick, and methods were proposed to tune surface wettability by altering the structure of the solid and the fluid at the interface.

At the device level, theory and experiments decipher the interdependence between the structure of the electric double layer and the structure of the fluid at the interface under dynamic conditions, a road map for optimising electrokinetic energy conversion. At the system level, the research focuses on wind energy conversion and harvesting solar thermal energy.

themes.name: Nanoconfined Fluids and Interfaces
themes.short: Molecular dynamics of water, ions, polymers and gases in nanochannels, carbon nanotubes and 2D-material membranes.
themes.text: Below a few nanometres, the wall decides how a fluid flows. Using molecular dynamics, we study how wettability, surface chemistry, roughness and ions control slip, structuring, capillary filling and diffusion of water in graphene nanochannels, carbon nanotubes and nanopores — from the slippery-to-sticky transition of hydrophobic channels and anomalous flow in sub-nanometre and angstrom-scale confinement, to polymers and brushes in confinement, selective graphene membranes for desalination, and molecular transport of gases in semiconductor fabrication lines.

themes.name: Electrokinetics and Nanofluidic Energy Harvesting
themes.short: Streaming potential, ion rectification, electroosmosis and DNA translocation, and turning flow into electricity.
themes.text: When a liquid moves past a charged surface it carries ions with it. We study this coupling between flow and charge — electric double layers, streaming potential, electroosmotic flow, ion rectification in polyelectrolyte- and zwitterion-coated nanochannels, programmable surface charge and DNA translocation — and use it to convert energy: electrokinetic energy harvesting over nanometre and sub-nanometre scales, carbonized cotton fibres with ultrahigh power density, and even electrokinetics in living plants.

themes.name: Heat Transfer and Thermal Management
themes.short: Microchannel heat sinks, nanofluids, boiling and cooling for electronics and batteries.
themes.text: Compact devices need to shed heat efficiently. We design microchannel heat sinks — tree-like branching networks, porous and double-layered channels — and study nanofluids with shape-engineered particles, non-Newtonian coolants, boiling on functionalized graphene and entropy-generation minimization, with applications in electronics cooling and battery thermal management.

themes.name: Droplets, Wetting and Smart Surfaces
themes.short: Drop impact, self-propulsion and water removal on textured, slippery and bio-inspired surfaces.
themes.text: Surface texture and wettability decide what a drop does. We study drop impact and touchdown on patterned and oil-infused slippery surfaces, wettability-driven self-propulsion of droplets, draining and meniscus dynamics, bio-inspired fog and water harvesting, wettability-guided self-assembly of Janus particles, and microstructured surfaces that remove water from PEM fuel cells.

themes.name: Multiphase and Non-Newtonian Flows
themes.short: Core–annular flow, jets, plugs, mixing and rheology in micro-, milli- and pipe-scale flows.
themes.text: Many energy and process applications involve two fluids or fluids with complex rheology. We study core–annular flow for energy-efficient transport of heavy oil, jets in cross-flow, nanofluid-induced production of monodispersed droplets and plugs, pulsatile and rheology-controlled mixing in T-channels, roughness effects in microchannels, and particle transport in ice-covered channels.

themes.name: Passive Cooling, Solar PV and Buildings
themes.short: Hydrogel cooling of photovoltaics, phase-change materials, façades and net-zero buildings.
themes.text: Interfacial ideas scale up to buildings and solar plants. We develop dual-function hydrogels for passive photovoltaic cooling and hybrid hydrogel–thermoelectric coolers, phase-change materials for PV panels and direct-gain walls, water-cooled and retrofitted glass façades, machine-learning-guided façade design, rooftop PV with battery dispatch, and pathways to net-zero energy buildings.

themes.name: Energy Storage and Functional Materials
themes.short: Pseudocapacitors, Li–S batteries, electrocatalysts and engineered composites.
themes.text: With materials collaborators we combine experiments with atomistic simulation to explain why new energy materials work: high-voltage and flexible pseudocapacitors with water-in-salt electrolytes, ZnS electrocatalysts for Li–S batteries, strain-activated metal–organic frameworks for water splitting, rubber–epoxy and liquid-phase-reinforced composites, and 3D-printed bio-inspired architectures.

themes.name: Machine Learning for Transport
themes.short: Physics-informed and data-driven models that speed up multiscale simulations.
themes.text: A thread running through the themes: neural networks trained on molecular simulations predict flow enhancement in nanochannels, physics-informed machine learning models electroosmotic flow for desalination membranes, and deep learning and data-driven optimisation are used for microchannel flows, battery cooling and building façades.

join.text: We are always looking for enthusiastic young minds to join the lab. The group is currently looking for interns who are proficient in coding.
routes: Admission is through IIT Kharagpur's PhD admission process (School of Energy Science and Engineering). Write to Dr. Bakli with your CV and research interests before applying.
Openings on sponsored projects are advertised on IIT Kharagpur's temporary jobs page.
Students proficient in coding (simulation, data analysis, machine learning) are welcome to write in with a CV and a short note on what they would like to work on.
We welcome collaborations with academic and industry partners. Contact Dr. Bakli directly.
